slot.brief: Given percentage composition of an organic compound and molar mass, find the molecular formula; simple ratio simplification to empirical formula.

stem: An organic compound contains $41.4\%$ carbon, $3.4\%$ hydrogen and $55.2\%$ oxygen. If its molar mass is $58\ \text{g mol}^{-1}$, find its molecular formula. Use atomic masses C = 12, H = 1 and O = 16.

verdicts.working: For 100 g: C:H:O = 41.4/12 : 3.4/1 : 55.2/16 ≈ 1:1:1, so the empirical formula is CHO (29 g mol⁻¹). The multiplier is 58/29 = 2, giving C₂H₂O₂.

working:
For $100$ g: $n_C=\dfrac{41.4}{12}=3.45$, $n_H=3.4$, $n_O=\dfrac{55.2}{16}=3.45$.
Ratio $C:H:O=1:1:1$; empirical formula $=\text{CHO}$.
Empirical formula mass $=29$; multiplier $=\dfrac{58}{29}=2$.
Molecular formula $=\text{C}_2\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$.

Independent check: For 100 g: C:H:O = 41.4/12 : 3.4/1 : 55.2/16 ≈ 1:1:1, so the empirical formula is CHO (29 g mol⁻¹). The multiplier is 58/29 = 2, giving C₂H₂O₂.
solution:
For $100\,\text{g}$, the mole ratio is $\frac{41.4}{12}:\frac{3.4}{1}:\frac{55.2}{16}=1:1:1$, so the empirical formula is $\text{CHO}$ (molar mass $29\,\text{g mol}^{-1}$).
$$n=\frac{58}{29}=2,\qquad \text{Molecular formula}=(\text{CHO})_2=\text{C}_2\text{H}_2\text{O}_2.$$
